sentences.text: Philosophical inquiry takes place through arguments about ethics, politics, metaphysics, knowledge, and the interpretation of inherited concepts.
Twentieth-century debate turned on what African philosophy is.

Placide Tempels's Bantu Philosophy (1945) presented the shared worldview of a people as a philosophy, an approach Paulin Hountondji made notorious as ethnophilosophy, faulting Tempels and his followers for casting African philosophy as an anonymous system of thought without individual thinkers.

claims.excerpt: casting African philosophy as an anonymous system of thought

sentences.text: Henry Odera Oruka's sage philosophy answered the same mistake by seeking the critical reflection of individual sages within traditional communities.

claims.excerpt: capable of the critical, second-order type of thinking about the various problems

sentences.text: Debates about ethnophilosophy ask whether shared beliefs can be presented as philosophy without identifying arguments and individual interlocutors.
Paulin Hountondji challenged the attribution of an anonymous collective doctrine to entire peoples, while Henry Odera Oruka investigated critical reflection among individual sages.
Their disagreements concern method, evidence, and intellectual agency.
Recurring themes include personhood and community.

Ifeanyi Menkiti argued that personhood is attained through participation in communal life, and Kwame Gyekye, who held that human beings are social by nature, counted individual liberty among the basic goods of a society while holding that duties take precedence over rights.

claims.excerpt: In this morality duties trump rights, not the other way around

sentences.text: Kwasi Wiredu called for the conceptual decolonization of African philosophy: concepts absorbed through colonial languages should be tested against intuitions in one's own language and kept or discarded on their merits.

claims.note: The test against one's own language is reported in Osha, not framed as a rule for every colonial concept.

sentences.text: Kwame Gyekye and Ifeanyi Menkiti advanced different accounts of personhood and communal life.
Discussions of ubuntu and related ethical vocabularies ask how relationships, dignity, responsibility, and autonomy interact.
